app.title: LHC Simulator
status.lost: Beam lost: orbit left the aperture
controls.title: Accelerator console
readout.title: Readouts
hint.energy.what: Energy of each proton. Injection from the SPS delivers 450 GeV; the RF cavities then raise it by about 5 GeV per second. The collision energy √s is twice the beam energy.
hint.field.what: The dipole magnets keep the protons on the ring. Their field must grow with the momentum: p = 0.2998 · B · ρ. In Auto mode the field follows the energy by itself. In Manual mode you drive it, and if it falls behind, the orbit shifts and the beam hits the wall.
hint.timeSpeed.what: How much game time passes per real second. The LHC ramp takes about 20 minutes, while collecting statistics for rare particles takes months.
hint.sqrtS.what: Hitting a fixed target wastes almost all the energy on moving the centre of mass, so √s grows only as the square root of the beam energy. Colliding beams give everything: √s = 2E. That is why the LHC is a collider.
footer.sources: Machine parameters: LHC Design Report. Masses: Particle Data Group.
beam.title: Beam and luminosity
beam.notColliding: No collisions: the beam must not be ramping
hint.bunches.what: How many proton bunches circulate in each beam. Luminosity grows linearly with the number of bunches. The LHC holds up to 2808 bunches spaced 25 ns apart.
hint.protons.what: How many protons each bunch contains. Luminosity grows with the square of this number, because every proton can hit every other. The design value is 1.15·10¹¹.
hint.betaStar.what: How hard the quadrupole magnets squeeze the beam at the collision point. Smaller β* means a smaller beam spot and more collisions. The design value is 0.55 m; Run 2 reached 0.25 m.
analysis.title: Analysis: μ⁺μ⁻ invariant mass
analysis.resetNote: Changing the pT threshold resets the data, like a new run with a different trigger.
hint.histogram.what: For every pair of muons the detector measures the momenta and we compute the invariant mass: the mass of a particle that could have decayed into them. Random pairs give a smooth background; a real particle gives a peak at its mass.
hint.window.what: Count the events inside a mass window. Estimate the background from two sidebands of the same total width, subtract it and divide by the square root of the background. Five sigma counts as a discovery.
hint.ptCut.what: Muons with low transverse momentum never reach the muon chambers, and a low threshold lets in many random pairs. A high threshold kills the light particles: a J/ψ gives muons of only 1.5 GeV each.
